summary: The biomarker follows an indirect response model in which the drug stimulates loss of the response: dR/dt = kout*R0 - kout*(1 + Smax*C/(SC50+C))*R. Estimates are R0 about 100.5, kout about 0.098 1/h, Smax about 8.4 and SC50 about 1.65 mg/L. It fit far better (fit5, BIC 69.3, sigma 3.1, no residual structure) than an inhibitory effect-compartment model (fit3, BIC 116.5; sigmoid version fit4, BIC 119.5) or indirect inhibition of production (fit2, BIC 124.0; Hill version fit7, BIC 120.5, nonidentifiable). Both of those left residual sigma at 7 or more, and fit2 and fit7 also trended with dose. Adding a Hill coefficient (fit6) gave n≈0.95 and a worse BIC.

summary: The biomarker is best explained by an indirect response model in which the drug inhibits its production: dR/dt = kin(1 - Imax*C/(IC50+C)) - kout*R, with R0 = 93.4, kout = 0.45 1/h, Imax = 0.93, IC50 = 0.24 mg/L (fit1, sigma 8.4, BIC 124.0). The dip nadir shifts later at lower dose (about 4 h at 500 mg, 12 h at 20 mg) and E rebounds to baseline, which the direct effect-compartment link cannot produce (fit2, sigma 29, systematic residuals). Alternatives with extra Hill steepness or an effect-compartment delay (fit3, fit4, fit5) did not improve BIC. Residuals still show a mild dose trend, so the model is adequate but not perfect; the IC50 is only moderately determined (27% SE), and because IC50 is well below the concentrations reached, predictions at 60 and 1000 mg are near saturated inhibition.

summary: Biomarker is produced at a zero-order-like rate inhibited by a delayed drug signal: dR/dt = E0*kout*(1 - Imax*A/(IC50+A)) - kout*R, with transit compartment dA/dt = ktr*(C - A), R(0)=E0, and C from the given one-compartment PK. summary: The biomarker is flat at E0 ≈ 49.8 (SE 1%, sigma ≈ 3.0) across both doses (20 and 200 mg) and all times up to 24 h. Dose-group means are identical (49.82 vs 49.80). Direct Emax (fit2), indirect-inhibition (fit3) and effect-compartment (fit4) models all fit no better than the null (BIC 47.7, 49.4, 48.6 vs 41.9) and their drug-effect parameters are non-identifiable or collapse to the no-effect limit. The data therefore show no detectable drug effect. Predicted biomarker at 60 and 1000 mg is the constant ~49.8, but this is an extrapolation with no observed exposure-response. Note: the 1000 mg prediction is outside the tested range.
label: pd_no_effect
